title: Expose six normal agent workflow tools
summary: Expose `wiki_state`, `wiki_decide`, `wiki_plan`, `wiki_implement`, `wiki_gate`, and `wiki_runtime` as normal agent tools while low-level primitives become compatibility aliases or internals.

goal.outcome: Agents see six normal workflow tools while existing low-level CodeWiki primitives remain safe compatibility aliases or internal use-case functions during migration.
acceptance: Pi adapter exposes `wiki_state`, `wiki_decide`, `wiki_plan`, `wiki_implement`, `wiki_gate`, and `wiki_runtime` as the normal internal agent tool surface.
`wiki_decide` orchestrates decision rows, approvals, KB mappings, and decision-build creation through existing diff-table/build primitives.
`wiki_plan` orchestrates roadmap/sprint alignment and planning-build creation through existing roadmap/build primitives.
`wiki_implement` records task-scoped TDD/code evidence and implementation-build creation without replacing normal file/code edit tools.
`wiki_gate` owns gateway preflight/validation and required linter/test evidence routing.
`wiki_runtime` owns session focus, leases, jobs, wait/wake, context boundaries, agency scheduling, and lifecycle/archive coordination.
Existing low-level tools remain available only as documented compatibility/expert aliases or are hidden internally; deprecation metadata and source-contract validation prevent accidental normal use.
README, skills, prompt contract, and source-contract snapshots agree on the six-tool target and compatibility policy.
non_goals: Do not remove low-level compatibility tools before wrapper parity and source-contract coverage exist.
Do not merge all behavior into one opaque mega-tool.
Do not change roadmap/build/validation JSON schemas except compatibility metadata needed for wrapper results.
Do not make bootstrap/config normal agent tools.
verification: wiki_gate/task-close linters for source-contract, stale-reference, changed, and alignment
